claims.text: Adding a small, optimized amount of a Si-based additive such as SiO2 to ZrB2 before spark plasma sintering at 1600–1700 °C will form an intergranular borosilicate glass phase.
The borosilicate grain-boundary phase will enhance densification at 1600–1700 °C.
The borosilicate grain-boundary phase will improve the mechanical integrity of ZrB2.
The borosilicate grain-boundary phase will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The borosilicate grain-boundary phase will improve resistance to corrosion by liquid plating metals.
The Si-based additive reacts with available boron and trace oxygen during spark plasma sintering to produce borosilicate.
The resulting borosilicate coats ZrB2 grain boundaries.
The intergranular phase reinforces grain bonding.
The intergranular phase acts as a physical barrier to oxygen ingress.
The intergranular phase acts as a physical barrier to liquid-metal attack.
Si-modified ZrB2 sintered at 1600–1700 °C will have densification comparable to or better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Si-modified ZrB2 sintered at 1600–1700 °C will have mechanical properties comparable to or better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Si-modified ZrB2 will have lower oxidation weight gain than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature ZrB2 without Si additives.
Si-modified ZrB2 will sustain less liquid-metal corrosion damage than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and lower-temperature ZrB2 without Si additives.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation above 2300 °C.
Unmodified lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to high-temperature oxidation.
Unmodified lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens are vulnerable to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
An argon atmosphere is applicable to synthesis involving Zr-containing diboride powders.
ZrB2 specimens can be fabricated by spark plasma sintering and characterized using Vickers hardness and oxidation measurements.
Vickers hardness alone evaluates the mechanical strength of the specimens.
